outcome: Sendov's conjecture (all n ≥ 2) and the stronger Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture were resolved: an AI-generated proof by GPT-5.6 Pro, curated and posted by Lech Mazur on 5 August 2026 and checked in Lean, was independently digested, simplified, verified, and re-formalized in Lean (sorry-free) by Terence Tao, who published a detailed exposition on 12 August 2026 confirming and extending the result.

ai.basis_quote: Recently, Lech Mazur was able to use an AI tool to resolve Sendov's conjecture for all n ≥ 2, with the proof verified in Lean.

summary: On 5 August 2026, Lech Mazur posted, via ProofAtlas, a proof of Sendov's conjecture for all polynomial degrees n ≥ 2, crediting OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Pro with producing the mathematical content of the argument (exploration, proof strategy, gap/error discovery) while Mazur served as curator, prompter and workflow designer who verified and checked the result in Lean (an initial ~90,000-line formalization). The ProofAtlas page itself flags this as an 'author-authorized early release' whose 'accepted-result review remains pending' — i.e., not yet digested by the field at that point. That digestion came a week later: on 12 August 2026 Terence Tao published 'A digestion of the proof of Sendov's conjecture,' in which he independently worked through the argument by hand (with what he describes as 'heavy AI assistance' in the exposition process), found it to rest on genuinely elementary complex analysis plus the Maclaurin inequality, streamlined it, and showed the same method resolves the strictly stronger Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture as well. Tao then produced his own from-scratch Lean 4 formalization (github.com/teorth/sendov, ~15,152 lines, verified sorry-free apart from the two intentional axiom-statement holes in Challenge.lean) using Claude Opus 5 as the formalization tool under his own mathematical direction. Because a leading expert (Tao) independently re-derived, checked, simplified, and exposed the full argument — which is the bar this dataset's rules set for 'resolved' rather than 'claimed' — I classify this as resolved, with the decisive event dated to Mazur's original 5 August 2026 posting (the first public written argument), noting Tao's confirmatory digestion five days later. The Wikipedia article on Sendov's conjecture has already been updated to reflect this. A follow-up preprint (Senjian An, arXiv:2609.04246, submitted 22 Aug 2026) gives an alternative proof of the same full result 'with reduced computer assistance,' building on the Mazur–Tao scalar reduction but replacing most of the computer verification with an analytic optimization argument; it does not mention any AI system in its own construction and is not needed for the resolved status, but corroborates that the underlying mathematical claim is being independently re-derived and is not fragile. AI role is coded 'generated' because, by Mazur's and ProofAtlas's own account, GPT-5.6 Pro produced the mathematical content of the original proof (the argument, not just formalization or proofreading) which Mazur and later Tao verified; a human did not produce the initial breakthrough. The subsequent Lean formalization work by Claude Opus 5 (under Tao) is a formalisation contribution and would, on its own, be coded 'none'/formalisation_only, but it is not the decisive event and does not change the ai_role of the resolving result.
competing_reading: One could argue for 'claimed' rather than 'resolved' on the grounds that ProofAtlas's own page states 'accepted-result review remains pending' and that, as of this research (22 Sept 2026), no formal journal acceptance or peer-reviewed publication has occurred — only a blog digestion and a Lean check, which some readers might not consider equivalent to journal-of-record acceptance. Against this: the dataset's own rule for 'resolved' explicitly allows 'an expert digestion that works through the proof' as sufficient, and Tao's post is exactly that — a leading expert independently re-deriving, checking, and re-formalizing the entire argument line by line, which is a stronger form of verification than most journal refereeing. I weighted the substance of Tao's digestion over ProofAtlas's own pending-review label, since the latter concerns ProofAtlas's internal editorial process, not whether the mathematical community's leading expert on this exact conjecture (who proved the n-sufficiently-large case himself in 2020) has verified it. A stricter reader could still classify this 'claimed' pending eventual journal publication.
what_would_settle_it: Formal journal acceptance/publication of either the Mazur–Tao result or An's independent proof, or further independent expert confirmation (e.g., another digestion, a second independent Lean formalization from scratch, or explicit endorsement by other specialists in the geometry-of-polynomials community) beyond Tao's single digestion.
